title: Why is the World's Best Tennis Player Worried About a Guy He's Beaten 9 Times in a Row?
summary: Imagine you're the best tennis player on the planet. You've beaten the same opponent nine times in a row—without even losing a single set! You'd feel pretty confident, right? Not if you're Jannik Sinner. The 24-year-old Italian is going for his second Wimbledon trophy in a row, but he says Sunday's final against Alexander Zverev is "going to be very, very tough." Wait, what? Why is the world number one so nervous? Because Zverev is a totally different player now. Last month, the 29-year-old German finally won his first Grand Slam at the French Open. It was his 41st try at a major tournament—that's like trying 41 times to beat the hardest level in a video game and finally winning! Sinner knows that winning a huge title changes everything. "He is a tough player to play against. He was before, but now even more," Sinner said. "He's very relaxed on court at the moment." Zverev agrees. "Once you win a major you know how to do it and you feel like you can do it again," he said. "You have this feeling inside of you." Sinner has been on fire this year, winning five Masters 1000 titles and crushing Novak Djokovic in the semifinals. But he also had a shocking loss at the French Open, where he collapsed in the heat and lost a match he was winning easily. Now he's bounced back, and he's ready for a battle. Both players have won over 40 matches this season—more than anyone else. It's a showdown between the two hottest players on tour. Will Sinner's winning streak continue, or will the new, confident Zverev finally break the spell? One thing's for sure: it won't be like their last nine meetings.
why_it_matters: Just like when a friend suddenly gets better at a video game and becomes hard to beat, even the world's best tennis player can worry about facing someone with fresh confidence.
